messages:
cheng: Heads up — noticed ~20% jump in p99 for hostside ingress after the kernel-selection rollout last night. CPU at the proxy spikes, tail latency looks correlated with many small writev/syscalls during stream forwarding. Can you all take a quick look?

sam: Oof. Do you have the flame graph or perf sample?

cheng: quick snapshot from the hot host: 

```
# perf top (ingress-proxy)
  writev/syscall  42.1%  <- many tiny writes
  http1_unwrap     18.4%
  proto_serialize  12.5%
  kv_cache_lookup   6.3%
  token_splitter    4.0%
```

Also p50/p95/p99 delta vs yesterday: `14ms / 52ms / 240ms` -> `15ms / 61ms / 290ms`.

liz: That layout smells like chunk boundary changes: earlier kernel selection change altered our mini-batching heuristic so tokenization produces more fragments. More fragments -> more writev -> syscalls spike.

perf-bot: New trace uploaded: https://perf.redwood/internal/trace/6123478901 (ingress-proxy -> grpc-gateway).

josh: Could be serialization too: http1 handler now marshals frames in smaller buffers before handing to proxy. Two quick mitigations: 1) coalesce small buffers in ingress proxy write path, 2) adjust batching heuristic in tokenization to prefer slightly larger fragments for long requests.

alex: FYI kvcache hit rate for route `/v1/generate` dropped ~8% after rollout. Query: `sum(rate(kv_gets{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (outcome)` shows increased misses. That could increase backpressure and amplification of syscall noise.

sam: Can we get a per-route writev count? I want to know if it's dominated by a few routes or all traffic.

cheng: On it. Running an aggregate metric now: `sum(rate(ingress_writev_calls[1m])) by (route)` — early results show top3 routes account for ~70% of writev count, `/v1/generate` is #1.

josh: Quick patch suggestion for proxy (local coalesce):

```
// pseudo
if (pending_bytes + next.len <= 4096) append_to_pending(next)
else flush_pending();
```

Should reduce syscall count without touching kernel heuristics. Low-risk canary.

liz: We should also instrument fragment size distribution at tokenization boundary. Add a histogram on token_fragment_size and a gauge for fragments_per_request.

ops-bot: Canary scheduled: ingress-proxy coalesce patch -> canary 10% at 6123480200. Alerting on p99 increase and writev count.

cheng: I'll throw a bisect job against the kernel-selection commit list too. If kvcache miss correlates with specific model variant, we might need to pin or change KV keying.

alex: One more datapoint: offline trace shows many small KV lookups clustered right after the token frontier change; could be tokenization emitting more prefixes and causing more cache lookups. If true, batching lookup or prefix coalescing may help a lot.

sam: Agreed. Short-term: deploy josh's coalesce, monitor writev/s and p99. Medium-term: adjust tokenization batching and kvcache lookup coalescing.

cheng: Patch uploaded: https://git.redwood/ingress-proxy/+/coalesce-small-writes. Rolling canary now. Will report back with metrics in 10m.

liz: Thanks — if canary looks good let's include a small test that asserts writev_count decreases for a synthetic long request.

ops-bot: Canary started. Canary metrics: writev_count @10%: -36% vs baseline, p99 @10%: -12% (initial).

cheng: Early positive signal. Continuing bisect. If anything regresses revert kernel selection.

josh: Nice. If coalesce isn't enough we can do a follow-up to accumulate until either 4k or end-of-frame.

alex: I'll open a follow-up ticket for kvcache coalesce and token-frag histogram.

cheng: Thanks all. Will update when bisect completes. :thumbsup:
